items: Two clear points where you step in, with a Done button. The Docs page has a new step 8 "Your turn" (the build waits for you) and the last step "Play and confirm". The agents write what only you can do into `OWNER-STEPS.md` with `owner_steps.py add setup ...`, stop, and wait with `owner_steps.py wait setup` until you press Done on every item; then they go on by themselves. At the end `owner_steps.py from-spec` writes one gameplay box for each player action of the game loop (action, rule, reward, end, replay), and only your press means it was played and works. Settings the agent checked during the build moved from the last step to the Build panel. A manual click on a step now holds for 45 seconds instead of being overridden by the running demo. The console's main page shows a "Your turn" card, and the Docs tab counter also counts blocked tasks that wait for you.

Misplaced devices are moved, not reported, and the demo scores with an egg. After each device the agent reads its place against the egg, the spawn area and the boundary and moves it when it is wrong. The first step of the build lists the actors, deletes the default player pads, keeps whatever the owner placed or configured by hand and writes it in `map/DEVICES.md`. The pen now scores the simple way the owner chose: a big egg prop with a damage volume that affects only creatures, and the elimination event of the chicken spawners gives the point (a capture area never fires for a chicken, which is why the score stayed at 0). The reference spec, plan, roadmap, playtest and `SCENERY.md` of the demo follow this.

Console design finished. The last 7 heavy animations (sweep, flash, stripes, ring, alert, hub beat, thinking dots) now move only transform and opacity; the 10 coloured side stripes became an underline on the selected tab, a tint, or nothing; every page has aligned numbers and a 65-character line limit; `ui_lint.py` prints `ui_lint: ok` on all eight pages. New `docs/console/PRODUCT.md` (who the console is for, what each page answers) and `docs/console/DESIGN.md` (colour meaning, measured contrast, type, motion, never-list). The manual chapter "The console" has a short section on how pages look and move.

A console that looks alive again. Neon in three tones on every page (`--neon-hi`, `--neon-mid`, `--neon-lo`), panels that breathe at their own rhythm, a light crossing the top of the page, pulsing "live" dots, a tick on changing numbers, and a pixel wave of translucent cubes over a panel whose data changes (fast or slow, random direction, off switch). Everything moves only transform and opacity; with reduced motion on, only brightness changes remain. `ui_lint` now checks that every page carries the shared blocks and the plain header.

The second brain, now a pillar and wired in. The philosophy and "How the kit thinks" explain what it holds (what worked, what did not, the lessons, the kit's own knowledge), who writes it, how the helpers read it and where it is weak. New and free (no AI tokens): `vault_check.py status|done` (which raw sources are new, changed or deleted since the last ingest, by content hash, with the pages that went stale), `quotes` (every quoted claim must exist word for word in the raw file it cites), `hot`; a SessionStart hook prints `wiki/hot.md` and the pending ingest, a PostToolUse hook runs the checks after every page written under `wiki/` (exit 2 sends the problems back in the same turn) via `Claude/hooks/brain_brief.py`, silent while the vault path is the placeholder. The vault template and the librarian now keep a `wiki/hot.md` cache and the ingest registry; rule 11 states the read order (hot, index, topic index, page; never for general coding questions).

A manual chapter and a picture for the second brain. New chapter "The second brain" (what it holds, five steps to turn it on, what happens in a session, the free checks with examples, where it is weak, what `/kit-doctor` says) and picture 13; the philosophy and "How the kit thinks" keep a short section that links to it.

Indigo and violet by default, and a console that fits a phone. Deep indigo surfaces with a Violet accent are the new default look on all pages and in the manual (the Cyan Aura is still one click away; the choice is stored again under a new key, so everyone starts from the new default). Every page now has a viewport tag; under 900px the header wraps and the tab bar scrolls inside itself, under 640px tables scroll inside their own box, touch screens get 40px controls. Before, Skills and News scrolled sideways on a phone and four pages had no viewport tag. `ui_lint` now fails a page without a viewport tag and warns when it has no narrow-screen rule; `console-ui` and `docs/console/DESIGN.md` carry the responsive, states and modes rules.

The exploration-lab agents no longer get the game's scenery. In the second run of the pilot, `/environment` handed the scenery to `mcp-level` because its description said "level work: place and edit actors and devices"; that agent is the guarded exploration lab, so the lab guard refused every write (no `Claude/LAB-PROJECT.txt`) and the demo stopped with an empty map. The descriptions of `mcp-level`, `mcp-build` and `mcp-material-vfx` now say "exploration lab only", and `/environment` and `/demo` say the game is built by the coder with direct MCP calls.
release.title: v1.114.0 — Study with the kit's knowledge, `/environment`, playtest checklist, the idea in the Docs page
